metadata.title: Causal Couture — Week 1: From Four Sources to One Prototype
metadata.methodological_boundary: Heuristic decision-support signals; not causal estimates or demand forecasts.

beats.narration_text: I’m Ushasvi Rachel, and this is Week 1 of Causal Couture—a four-part progress series for Humanitarians.ai. This week was about integration: bringing the project’s earlier data architecture and analytical components together into a functioning end-to-end prototype.

shot.visual_intent: Ushasvi Rachel branded Week 1 opening; four inputs converge on one prototype.

show.event: Reveal Causal Couture Progress · 1 of 4.
Reveal Ushasvi Rachel and Humanitarians.ai.
Four source nodes converge into one prototype node.

beats.narration_text: The starting point was four separate categories of fashion-business data: sales, inventory, social engagement, and web activity. Each represented a different part of the business. Week 1 began by bringing those sources into one analytical workflow.

shot.visual_intent: Four isolated source-category cards, with no fabricated schemas or values.

show.event: Reveal Sales and Inventory as separate cards.
Reveal Social Engagement and Web Activity.
Draw a boundary around all four as the Week 1 starting point.

beats.narration_text: The first step was integrating those four source datasets. Sales and inventory described commercial activity and product availability. Social engagement and web activity added signals about attention and online behavior. Together, they provided the inputs for the prototype.

shot.visual_intent: Four labeled inputs flow into a single ingestion boundary.

show.event: Send Sales and Inventory toward ingestion.
Send Social Engagement and Web Activity toward ingestion.
All four arrive at Prototype Inputs.

beats.narration_text: Integration alone was not enough. The ingestion and preprocessing workflow also had to standardize the sources and prepare them for downstream analysis. That created a consistent path from incoming data through validation and preprocessing, without assuming that the original sources already shared one structure.

shot.visual_intent: Schema-like flow through validation, standardization, and preprocessing without invented rules.

show.event: Show differently shaped abstract records entering.
Records pass through Validation.
Records pass through Standardization and Preprocessing.
Consistent abstract records emerge.

beats.narration_text: After preprocessing, the sources were combined into a unified analytical dataset at the date-by-SKU level. That common grain connected different business signals around the same product and date, giving the analytical layer one consistent foundation.

shot.visual_intent: Four standardized streams merge into a date × SKU grid; only date and SKU are concrete keys.

show.event: Four standardized streams approach a grid.
Grid keys Date and SKU lock into place.
Label the result Unified Analytical Dataset.

beats.narration_text: From that unified dataset, I began building the decision-support feature layer. One group represented sales and demand activity. Another captured inventory availability and low-stock conditions. These features described pressure on demand and possible risk on the stock side.

shot.visual_intent: Unified dataset branches to demand activity, inventory availability, and low-stock conditions.

show.event: Branch to Sales and Demand Activity.
Branch to Inventory Availability.
Add Low-Stock Conditions.
Group all three under Decision-Support Features.

beats.narration_text: The feature layer also included social engagement and web conversion behavior, along with sales and social spikes, sell-through behavior, and view-to-cart conversion. At this stage, these were analytical signals derived from the integrated data—not causal effects and not forecasts.

shot.visual_intent: Five additional labeled feature-family branches, ending with a non-causal/non-forecast boundary.

show.event: Reveal Social Engagement and Web Conversion Behavior.
Reveal Sales and Social Spikes.
Reveal Sell-Through and View-to-Cart.
Frame all as Analytical Signals; show Not causal effects · Not forecasts.

beats.narration_text: Those features supported the Phase 3 heuristic business scorecard. The scorecard organized the available information into four primary signals: Demand Pressure, Stock Risk, Engagement Momentum, and Conversion Strength.

shot.visual_intent: Feature families collapse into four named heuristic scorecard quadrants.

show.event: Feature-family labels compress toward a scorecard.
Reveal Demand Pressure and Stock Risk.
Reveal Engagement Momentum and Conversion Strength.
Label the whole Heuristic Business Scorecard.

beats.narration_text: The four signals were then combined into an overall score and a rule-based recommendation. The purpose was to translate several analytical signals into an output that could be easier to interpret as business decision support.

shot.visual_intent: Four scorecard signals converge into Overall Score and Rule-Based Recommendation, with no values or rules invented.

show.event: Four named signals converge.
Reveal Overall Score as an abstract output.
Reveal Rule-Based Recommendation.
Bracket both as Business Decision Support.

beats.narration_text: The next step was connecting the analytical workflow to an interactive frontend. Python and FastAPI provided the API layer. The data-processing workflow used tools including Pandas, Polars, CSV and Parquet data structures, and DuckDB-related architecture.

shot.visual_intent: Code-oriented architecture from data processing through Python/FastAPI to an unspecified interactive frontend.

show.event: Reveal analytical/data-processing workflow with supported tool labels.
Draw Python + FastAPI API boundary.
Connect API to a generic Interactive Frontend frame.

beats.narration_text: By the end of the week, the broader workflow could move from source data through validation and preprocessing, into the unified dataset, then through the analytical scorecard and recommendation layer, and finally to the interactive frontend.

shot.visual_intent: Complete supported pipeline lights up chronologically.

show.event: Light Source Data, Validation, and Preprocessing in order.
Light Unified Dataset.
Light Analytical Scorecard and Recommendation.
Light Interactive Frontend and label End-to-End Prototype.

beats.narration_text: But the methodological boundary matters. These Phase 3 scores were heuristic decision-support signals. They were not causal estimates, and they were not demand forecasts. The prototype could organize and summarize the available signals, but it could not establish cause and effect or predict future demand.

shot.visual_intent: Three-column methodological boundary: completed heuristic support versus two explicitly unavailable claim types.

show.event: Reveal Heuristic Decision Support as the completed lane.
Reveal Causal Estimates as Not Yet.
Reveal Demand Forecasts as Not Yet.
Restate No cause-and-effect claim · No future-demand prediction.

beats.narration_text: The Week 1 output was a working Phase 3 end-to-end analytical prototype: four source categories, one unified analytical dataset, a business-signal scorecard, a rule-based recommendation layer, an API, and an interactive frontend. Next: extending the prototype into the next analytical phase.

shot.visual_intent: Completed Week 1 components assemble into one prototype card, followed by the exact approved next-phase transition.

show.event: Recap four sources and unified dataset.
Add scorecard, recommendation, and API.
Add interactive frontend; lock Working Phase 3 Prototype.
Reveal: Next: extending the prototype into the next analytical phase.
